item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00419","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C23","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C05 is a strong reusable template: both proclamations commemorate the anniversary of a major American figure, develop an extended account of that figure's life and national contribution, connect the commemoration to civic principles, and culminate in a call to observe a year-long period through appropriate activities and ceremonies. The operative language and sequence are substantially closer than ordinary commemorative-proclamation boilerplate. C23 shares the person-centered centennial-year mechanism but is much shorter and less textually parallel. C18 shares an honored historical figure and ceremonial observance, but only for a single annual day.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"call upon the American people to observe the one hundredth anniversary of Theodore Roosevelt's birth throughout the centennial year beginning October 27, 1957, by appropriate activities and ceremonies","parent_excerpt":"call upon all officials and agencies of Federal Government, and upon all citizens, to observe the year commencing January 11, 1957, as the Alexander Hamilton Bicentennial, and to do honor to his memory during the period with appropriate activities and ceremonies","explanation":"Distinctively parallel operative language establishes a year-long anniversary observance for a historic statesman and prescribes appropriate activities and ceremonies."},{"child_excerpt":"Theodore Roosevelt loved America with impassioned devotion and served her greatly in public office and as a private citizen.","parent_excerpt":"Alexander Hamilton served his country well throughout his life","explanation":"Both begin the substantive tribute by presenting the commemorated figure's lifelong national service, followed by an extended catalog of accomplishments."},{"child_excerpt":"by the study of his life and teachings, and above all, by individual, personal rededication to those responsibilities of American citizenship","parent_excerpt":"a happy opportunity for all of us to think afresh of his sincere efforts and inspiring leadership in the work of the men who laid the foundations, raised the structure, and built the sustaining traditions of the Government of the United States","explanation":"Both turn historical commemoration into contemporary civic reflection and rededication, reinforcing the shared functional structure beyond generic ceremonial language."}]}
